newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK protesters seek higher elderly welfare payments.
newsitem.headline: HK protesters seek higher elderly welfare payments.

text.p: Hundreds of protesters and leading politicians took to the streets in Hong Kong on Sunday to demand an immediate rise in social security payments to the elderly.

About five hundred elderly people and political party representatives demonstrated outside government offices in Central District on Sunday, calling for an increase of HK$300 ($38.50) in welfare payments to HK$2,900 a month.
Democratic Party representative Fred Li said his group would vote against the budget if the government did not agree to immediately increase the payment, government radio reported.

"I think the message is strong and hopefully the Financial Secretary will respond to our request when he has a chance to stand up and speak at this Wednesday's Legco sitting," he said, referring to the next session of the territory's Legislative Council.
Passage of the budget is virtually assured despite protests that growth in social welfare spending fell to 9.1 percent from 20.8 percent last year.
The Legislative Council will be abolished on July 1 and is being replaced by the Beijing-approved Provisional Legislature.
China participated in the creation of the 1997/98 budget straddling the return of the territory to Chinese control at midnight on June 30.
